title: Chats run through /goal (and scheduled reminders) never get memory and are never indexed
body:
**Problem** (high)
In dsh 0.2.1-rc.5, `/goal <objective>` is a command, not a user message. dsh then drives the work as follow-up turns whose message has `source.kind: 'goal'`, and the user's objective sits inside that text as `Objective: "..."`. Scheduled reminders arrive the same way with `source.kind: 'schedule'`. The plugin treats only `kind: 'user'` as human input, so for this kind of work: (a) the prompt is empty, so no chat list, no topic hits and no inlined source are ever added; (b) the rounds are not counted as turns, so a goal chat with 0 human turns is never indexed, however many rounds it runs (default limit 256). Part (b) looks like #42, but the cause differs: a fix for #42 that still counts `kind: 'user'` turns would not index these chats, and part (a) has nothing to do with #42. Goal and schedule are both in the standard preset.

**Where**: src/host/memory.js:26 and :95 (the prompt is built only from source.kind 'user'), src/core/session.js:9 (isHuman), src/host/builder.js:103 (needs span.userTurns >= buildEveryTurns)

**Evidence**
dsh code: dsh-goal-round-driver/lib/index.js lines 142-165 build each round with createUserMessage({ content: renderGoalRoundPrompt(goal, round), source: { kind: "goal", goalId, revision, round } }) and send it with agent.followup; lines 10-16 put `Objective: ${JSON.stringify(goal.objective)}` in the text. dsh-command-goal/lib/index.js lines 96-106 send a kind 'user' message only when attachments come with the command. dsh-schedule/lib/index.js line 1594 sends reminders with `source: { kind: "schedule" }`.
Reproduced in the real runtime: cordis + dsh-llm/session/session-projection/system-prompt/tools/agent/agent-loop + dsh-commands + dsh-goal + dsh-goal-round-driver + dsh-command-goal, with a scripted provider and the repo plugin loaded (<scratch>/cg-c4-real/drive6.mjs). First an indexed chat about commit signing was built. Then `/goal set up commit signing with gpg for this repo, like we did before` ran 6 rounds. Results: user/message sources ["goal"x6]; 0 of 6 model requests carried a [context-graph] block; the chat has no meta.json, so it was never indexed. Control: the same words typed as a normal message got sources ["user","context-graph"].
In the same runtime these contracts all matched dsh (drive1-5): the pre-step waterfall and next(), turn-stopping, status/created/inbox-discarded events, header fields, session/title, cross-chat turn recall through sessionQuery, the command with input.hint, defineTool, the builder's llm.stream call at the lowest reasoning effort ('off' on DeepSeek), and isAgentLoopRequest.

**Fix**
Treat a goal round as a prompt: match on its parsed objective, once per goal revision (shown.ids already stops repeats). Count goal (and schedule) rounds toward buildEveryTurns. Keep privacy: a goal whose /goal command ran inside an off stretch is private, rounds included.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (real-dsh lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Reproduced on my own in the real runtime (cg-c4-real-dsh/v0.mjs: dsh-commands, dsh-goal, dsh-goal-round-driver and dsh-command-goal with the repo plugin). The dsh log shows `command/run` (source user, args = objective), then 5 user/message events with kind 'goal'. That is 5 turns and 5 model requests, 0 of them with a [context-graph] block. No meta.json was written, so the chat was never indexed. A forced `/context-graph build` read 5 assistant messages, 0 user messages and no objective. So even an indexed goal chat loses the user's request, which a #42 fix that counts kind 'user' turns would not change. Control: the same words typed as a message got sources [user, context-graph] and 1 block. dsh code confirms the cause. The round driver uses createUserMessage with source kind 'goal' and puts the objective in the text. command-goal sends a kind 'user' message only with attachments, and …_

title: Plans approved in plan mode and the user's ask_user answers never reach indexing or turn recall
body:
**Problem** (medium)
In dsh 0.2.1-rc.5 the two most decision-heavy things in a chat travel through tools. Plan mode hands over the complete markdown plan only as the `plan` argument of `exit_plan_mode`; the tool result is a fixed sentence. The user's answers to `ask_user_question` come back as a JSON tool result. The builder indexes only human prompts and assistant text, and turn recall shows only `[tools: exit_plan_mode]`. So the approved plan and the user's chosen options never become topics, and `recall("c3t7")` of that turn returns neither. Both tools are in the standard preset (plan-mode group, tool-ask-user).

**Where**: src/core/session.js:47-49 (collectSpan reads only text blocks of assistant/message), :216-224 (turnTranscript keeps only tool names)

**Evidence**
dsh code: dsh-plan-mode/lib/index.js lines 233-237 define parameters `plan` ("The complete plan, as markdown..."); lines 247-250 render the result as "Plan approved — plan mode exited; carry out the plan starting with your next step.". dsh-tool-ask-user/lib/index.js lines 299-302 render `JSON.stringify({answers})`.
Reproduced in the real loop with stand-in tools that use dsh's names, parameters and result text (drive7.mjs). The builder input (2,358 chars) contains the plan: false. It contains the user's answer 'Postgres 16 ... pgbouncer in transaction mode': false. The plan step's assistant content is ["tool-call"] (the plan lives only in tool/call arguments, 184 chars). turnTranscript of that turn is the prompt, `[tools: exit_plan_mode]` and "OK."

**Fix**
In collectSpan and turnTranscript, add the `plan` argument of exit_plan_mode tool-call blocks as assistant text, and the selected/custom answers from ask_user_question results as user text. Other tool output stays out (#47); off-stretch gaps apply by seq as usual.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (real-dsh lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Reproduced with the REAL dsh-plan-mode, dsh-user-questions and dsh-tool-ask-user, not stand-ins (v1.mjs; a listener on user-questions/request answers). `/plan Design the database layer...` led to ask_user_question, whose tool result is {answers:[{id:'db',selected:['Postgres 16 with pgbouncer in transaction mode']}]}. Then exit_plan_mode was approved: plan mode left, result 'Plan approved — plan mode exited...'. Its assistant content is only a tool-call block; the plan is the 177-char argument. The builder input (2,418 chars) contains the plan: false, and the user's answer: false. collectSpan turn 1 is only the prompt plus 'OK.'. turnTranscript t1 is the prompt, '[tools: ask_user_question, exit_plan_mode]' and 'OK.'. dsh's own plan-mode section says 'Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply', so the plan exists only in the tool argument. An answer given later instead returns as user/…_

title: Turn ids (t7 / c3t7) do not match dsh's own turn numbers
body:
**Problem** (low)
dsh numbers turns by turn/start (data.turn), and its turn navigation shows those numbers ('Turn {turn}' / '第 {turn} 轮'). The plugin counts kind 'user' messages instead. So a steer typed while the agent works counts as a new turn although dsh keeps it inside the same turn. Goal rounds, scheduled reminders and wake-up turns are not counted, although dsh counts them. When a user takes 'turn 7' from dsh's navigation, or compares the page's (t7) labels with it, recall("c3t7") returns a different turn; in a goal-only chat every t-id is missing.

**Where**: src/core/session.js:46 (turn: humans.length), :195-201 (turnTranscript counts human prompts); shown to users as (tN) on the page (src/client/client.js:290) and in source labels

**Evidence**
Real-runtime repro (drive5b.mjs): one followup, a steer during its tool step, then one more prompt. dsh turn/start numbers are 1,2. The plugin's t1 is the first prompt, t2 is the steer inside dsh turn 1, and t3 is dsh's turn 2. In the goal chat of drive6, dsh has 6 turns and the plugin finds none. dsh UI strings: dsh-client-ui-chat/lib/client.js lines 5802-5805 (chat.turnNavigation.turn '第 {turn} 轮'), fed by dsh-session-turn-outline, which uses turn/start.

**Fix**
Number messages by the data.turn of the enclosing turn/start, and serve turn N as the events between turn/start N and the next turn/start. Convert stored `t` values at the next build (they can be recomputed from each message's seq in the log).

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (real-dsh lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Reproduced (v2.mjs): one followup, a steer typed during a running tool step, a second prompt, /goal with 2 rounds, then a third prompt. dsh has turns 1-5; the plugin finds t1-t4 and no t5. dsh turn 1 splits into plugin t1 (the prompt and '[tools: slow]', with no answer) and t2 (the steer and the answer). dsh turn 2 is t3, which also takes in the answers of goal turns 3-4. dsh turn 5 is t4. dsh's turn numbers survive a resume (turnBoundary projection), and the README calls c3t7 'Turn 7 of chat 3 from dsh's log', so the mismatch is real. The impact is small: the plugin's labels and recall use the same count, so the model's own lookups stay consistent. dsh shows the number only in the rail's aria-labels and in the tooltip of turns without a prompt, such as goal rounds. The visible side effects: recall of a steered turn returns the question without its answer, and goal rounds are folded int…_

title: Skip the full dsh-log read that learnForkPoint does on the first recall of every ordinary chat
body:
**Problem** (low)
learnForkPoint is meant for forks whose meta was written by v0.4-v0.6 and has no forkSeq. But ordinary chats never get forkSeq either, so the first recall of any other chat in an app run, topic recalls included, calls sessionQuery.observeSession and loads that chat's whole dsh log just to learn it is not a fork. A topic recall otherwise needs only the plugin's small files. A meta written by 0.9.0 carries firstKey (0.8.0 metas carry firstPrompt), and those versions always set forkSeq on a fork in the same write. So such a meta already says whether the chat is a fork.

**Where**: src/host/recall.js:40-45 (learnForkPoint) and :184

**Evidence**
Measured in the real runtime with dsh-session-persistence-jsonl (zstd, as in ~/.dsh/sessions) and dsh-session-query. Two cold 120-turn chats of about 530 KB on disk were used (drive8d.mjs, with observeSession timed). First topic recall: 41.4 ms and 25.3 ms, of which observeSession took 37.9 ms and 22.7 ms. The next topic recall of the same chat: 2.2 ms and 2.0 ms. For scale, the owner's real logs (file sizes only): 46 files, largest 295 KB, 4.2 MB in total.

**Fix**
In learnForkPoint, also return false when view.meta.firstKey or view.meta.firstPrompt is defined. Before: 25-41 ms for the first topic recall per chat per run. After: about 2 ms (the fork-point-known path). Turn recalls still read the log once in sharedTurn, which already records the fork point.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (real-dsh lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Re-measured in fresh app runs (v3build.mjs, then v3recall.mjs, 5 runs) with the real dsh-session-persistence-jsonl (zstd) and dsh-session-query. I used 4 indexed chats of 40, 86, 149 and 295 KB on disk; the owner's 46 real logs (sizes only) are median 60 KB, p90 169 KB, max 295 KB. An ordinary chat's meta has firstKey and no forkSeq. Each chat's first topic recall in a run calls observeSession once. The first recall in a run took 43-62 ms in total (observe 37-53 ms); first recalls of the other chats took 12-31 ms (observe 10-31 ms). What remains without the observe is 2-9 ms, and the next recall of the same chat takes 0.7-2.1 ms with no observe. The shortcut is safe in code. v0.8.0's initialMeta wrote firstPrompt together with forkSeq, and every write went through withForkPoint. v0.9.0 adds firstKey in upToDate inside withForkPoint. A recovered (damaged) meta could lose forkSeq but is f…_

title: A file the model reads can hide real topics, and the same scan is the slowest per-message step in long chats
body:
**Problem** (low)
shownContext runs the RECALLED topic-line regex over every tool/result on the surface. RECALL_RESULT only decides whether the tokens are counted. So any tool output with a line like '- c3n12 ...' marks that id as already shown, and the topic is never sent in that chat while the output stays on the surface. A file read or a command's output is enough. This goes against the function's own doc: ids should come only from 'the plugin's blocks, or fetched with recall ... an example id cannot hide a real topic (#51)'. The owner's own README.md has four such lines (39, 40, 145, 147: c3n12, c3n4, c2n1, c1n3), so in the owner's workspace any chat that reads README.md loses those four topics. Second effect: the regex reads the full text of every tool output on every human turn, on the critical path.

**Where**: src/core/session.js:118-121 (shownContext, tool/result branch), called on every human turn from src/host/memory.js:105 before the request goes out

**Evidence**
Harness repro <scratch>/cg-c4-tokens/m8-repro-shown.mjs. Chat A is built (topic c1n1 'commit signing'). Chat B asks 'how do we do commit signing with gpg?' and gets a block with the inline source. The same chat after one tool/result 'Memory export:\n- c1n1 example line...' gets no block. Timing in m7-shown-fix.mjs, surface of 200 turns x 10 tool results of 10 KB (4,801 events, ~22 MB): 16.3 ms per human turn now, 1.4 ms with the fix. At 50 turns: 4.8 -> 0.5 ms. Ids now [c3n12,c2n3,c4n1], with the fix [c3n12,c2n3]; c4n1 came from a fixture-like file read. Counted tokens are equal (510/510). For scale, the whole pre-step at 150 chats is 6.6 ms (m2-cpu.mjs). Full suite with the fix: 216/216.

**Fix**
One line in the tool/result branch: `if (!RECALL_RESULT.test(text)) continue` before counting tokens and scanning ids. Every recall output starts with '# c3', '# t7' or '[context-graph]', so recalls keep counting.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (tokens-quality lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Confirmed, but the trigger is narrower than claimed. session.js:121 runs RECALLED over every tool/result. RECALL_RESULT only gates the token count. Harness repro (cg-c4-tokens-quality/v0-shown.mjs, chat A topic c1n1, question about commit signing with gpg): with no tool result, the block is sent. Raw `cat` output, a git-diff context line ' - c1n1 ...' or a '# c1n1 ' heading each give shown ids [c1n1] and no block. dsh's own read tool does NOT trigger it: dsh-tool-fs formatReadOutput numbers every line ('39: - c3n12 ...'), and `grep -n` output doesn't either. So 'any chat that reads README.md' holds only for shell reads (cat, Get-Content, sed) or git diff/show. The speed half is minor at real context sizes (v0-time.mjs): 0.45 MB surface (about a 128K-token window) 0.59 -> 0.03 ms; 4 MB 4.8 -> 0.6 ms; 20 MB 26 -> 0.5 ms. Gating ids by RECALL_RESULT is safe: every ok recall output starts w…_

title: An exact camelCase identifier finds nothing, while the same identifier in snake_case finds its topic
body:
**Problem** (medium)
The README says identifiers yield their parts ('clear_conversation also yields clear and conversation') and an exact identifier counts double. isCode only recognises _ . and slashes, and searchUnits lowercases before splitting. So useMemoryStore or isAgentLoopRequest is one plain word: 2 points, below the floor of 3, with no parts. A question that names the exact identifier never reaches its topic. lowerCamel is how dsh and this plugin (JS) name things.

**Where**: src/core/text.js:107-110 (isCode) and 124/139-150 (text lowercased before words are looked at)

**Evidence**
<scratch>/cg-c4-tokens/m3-quality.mjs: a chat of 8 topics labelled with JS identifiers (useMemoryStore hook rewrite, isAgentLoopRequest identity check, createUserMessage source kind, readJsonCached stat key, fetchWithTimeout wrapper, getServerSideProps data loading, ...) and 8 questions naming them ('where do we call useMemoryStore', 'why does isAgentLoopRequest return false', 'the memory store hook rerenders too often'). Now: 0/8 found. Same topics and questions in snake_case: 6/6. With the fix: 8/8, precision 1.0. The corpus does not move: TARGETED 20/20 top-1 20, HELD_T 10/10, UNRELATED 0 blocks, HELD_U 1 block. All 84 core+store tests pass. Full suite with this fix plus the next two: 216/216 (copy in <scratch>/cg-c4-tokens/repo-pc).

**Fix**
Take each word from the NFKC text before lowercasing. A lowerCamel word of 7+ letters/digits (/^[a-z][a-z0-9]*[A-Z]/) becomes { kind:'word', tokens:[lower, ...hump parts], code:true }, the same shape snake_case gets today. PascalCase stays a plain word, so GitHub, JavaScript or DeepSeek do not count double. Known limit: brand words like eCommerce count as code. Tested patch: <scratch>/cg-c4-tokens/variants/camel/text.js

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (tokens-quality lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Confirmed with my own set (v12-quality.mjs): 8 topics with lowerCamel labels such as loadViews, matchAcross, isSubagent and setInterval, plus questions, inside the 60-topic corpus. HEAD finds 4/8: it hits only when the question has a second label word or two gist words. The same topics in snake_case find 8/8. The proposed camel split finds 8/8, precision 1.0. Corpus unchanged: TARGETED 20/20 top-1 20, HELD_T 10/10, UNRELATED 0, HELD_U 1. Full suite 216/216 in my copy with the camel+plural text.js (repo-fix). Side effect: camel parts also become label words on the topic side, so the corpus alias pathToFileURL turns 'can you share a file url to my phone' into a hit on c5n7 (1 of my 10 unrelated prompts gets a block; HEAD gives 0). snake_case behaves the same today, but this is a new false-positive path; counting camel parts as gist-only on the topic side would avoid it. 16 KB paste at 9,0…_

title: Singular and plural forms never match; folding plurals roughly triples recall on reworded questions at no cost
body:
**Problem** (medium)
Matching is exact per word, so 'versions'/'version', 'tests'/'test', 'queries'/'query', 'dags'/'dag', 'columns'/'column' are different words. A question worded with the other number misses a label word and falls under the floor. Folding plurals on both sides (topics and messages use the same searchUnits) fixes it without loosening the gate.

**Where**: src/core/text.js:139-150 (searchUnits word loop)

**Evidence**
<scratch>/cg-c4-tokens/m3-quality.mjs, EN_INFLECT: 20 questions written before testing, each worded with another inflection than its topic ('which node versions do the tests run against' -> 'Node version test matrix', 'which queries get logged as slow', 'when do the airflow dags run', 'what type do we use for timestamp columns'). Now: 4/20 found. Plural folding: 11/20 (precision 0.92). Unchanged: TARGETED 20/20 top-1 20, HELD_T 10/10, UNRELATED 0 blocks, HELD_U 1, Chinese 11/16. Core+store tests 84/84; full suite 216/216 together with the camel fix. Matching cost over 9,000 topics (m4-perf-variant.mjs): ordinary message 2.5 -> 2.2 ms, 16 KB paste 5.9 -> 7.2 ms. Also folding -ing/-ed reaches 13/20 but fails 2 tests: a traceback matches 'Self-hosted runner' through hosted->host. So fold plurals only.

**Fix**
const stem = (w) => { if (w.length < 4 || !/^[a-z]+$/.test(w)) return w; let s = w; if (/ies$/.test(s) && s.length > 4) s = s.slice(0, -3) + 'y'; else if (/(?:ches|shes|sses|xes|zes)$/.test(s)) s = s.slice(0, -2); else if (/[^su]s$/.test(s)) s = s.slice(0, -1); return STOPWORDS.has(s) ? w : s }. Apply it to plain words (tokens: [stem(raw)]) and to compound parts, never to the whole compound or code identifier. Known limit: 'cookies' folds to 'cooky' and still misses 'cookie' (it misses today too). Patch: <scratch>/cg-c4-tokens/variants/plural/text.js

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (tokens-quality lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Confirmed with my own 12 questions, each worded in the other number from its label (api keys, feature flags, docker images, unit tests, cron jobs, sessions, templates, dependencies, budgets, migrations, signatures, caches). HEAD 1/12, plural folding 11/12, precision 0.85. The extra hits are related: c1n4 for docker build, c5n8 for node --test. Corpus metrics unchanged; 0 blocks on my 10 unrelated prompts. The one miss is a flaw in the proposed stem(): 'caches' becomes 'cach' while 'cache' stays 'cache', because the -ches/-shes/-xes rule also strips -es from singulars ending in e (caches, niches). Cost at 9,000 topics, separate processes, median: ordinary message 3.3-3.7 -> about 4.6 ms; 16 KB paste about 7.8 ms, unchanged within noise. Suite 216/216 with the fix._

title: Every new chat gets the ~190-token chat list, even when its first message has nothing to do with memory
body:
**Problem** (low)
The list is sent on the first turn whatever the first message says. Everywhere else, rule 3 'evidence before tokens' applies. The list then stays in the chat and is re-sent as cached input with every later request; the plugin's own ledger charges that as resent. Its order is good: for 30/30 targeted first messages the right chat leads (m14-order.mjs), so only the unconditional sending wastes tokens.

**Where**: src/host/memory.js:115-124 (top layer on the first turn); src/core/render.js:94-111

**Evidence**
Harness at 150 chats (<scratch>/cg-c4-tokens/m13-first.mjs): 30/30 unrelated first messages (UNRELATED + HELD_U) got a block. 29 of them got only the list. Total 5,755 tokens, mean 192 per chat, plus about 19 tokens of cached re-send per later request (0.1 x 192 in the ledger's weights). The header alone is 47 tokens (m1-list.mjs).

**Fix**
Send the list together with the chat's first block (topic hits or a day digest), or when the first message asks about earlier work (asksAboutPast). Keep it once per chat as now. Measured effect: unrelated first messages 5,755 -> 0 tokens; targeted first messages unchanged, since all 30 get hits. A softer gate (some chat shares a label or summary word with the message) would still list for 13 of the 30 unrelated messages and save 2,992 of 5,348 tokens at 54 chats (m1-list.mjs). Trade-off for the owner: a vague opener like 'let us continue the CI work' would no longer see the list.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (tokens-quality lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Token numbers reproduced (v3-list.mjs). For the 30 UNRELATED+HELD_U first messages, the list goes to all 30, and 29 get nothing else. 6 chats: 5,710 tokens (mean 190). 150 chats: 5,342 (mean 178). The header is 47 tokens. Through the harness with a single earlier chat, 'what is a good name for my new puppy' still gets a 70-token list. Caveat: sending the list once per chat is deliberate (#26/#27, architecture table). It is also the only pointer to earlier chats when a first message has no matching words ('continue where we left off'), so gating it by evidence gives up that case, which nobody measured. Gain per chat: about 180-190 tokens once plus about 19 cached per later request._

title: recall of a day has no budget: up to 3,600 tokens where the other recall layers stop at 1,000-2,000
body:
**Problem** (low)
Topic recall shares 1,000 tokens, turn recall is capped at 2,000, and chat recall is bounded by 40 lines plus 600 tokens. A day recall lists up to 10 topic lines for each of up to 10 chats. The day digest in memory.js already uses rangeMaxChats/rangeMaxTopics = 3/3. Every topic left out is still named ('... N more from then: recall("c3")'), so smaller caps hide nothing.

**Where**: src/host/recall.js:178 (renderRange called without caps, so its defaults of 10 chats x 10 topics apply); src/core/render.js:142

**Evidence**
<scratch>/cg-c4-tokens/m10-day.mjs and m1-list.mjs, corpus chats all active on one day. 6 chats: 2,170 tokens now, 886 with 3 topics a chat. 12 chats: 3,633 tokens (112 lines) now, 1,487 with 3 topics a chat. For comparison, topic recall over the 60 corpus topics: mean 386, max 1,072 tokens (m9-recall.mjs, real tool at 150 chats).

**Fix**
renderRange(views, range, { maxChats: 10, maxTopics: cfg.rangeMaxTopics }) in recall.js, or a separate recallDayTopics: 3. That is -59% on a busy day, and the model drills down with recall("c<chat>").

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (tokens-quality lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Reproduced exactly (v5-day.mjs, corpus chats all active on one local day). 6 chats: 2,170 tokens -> 886 with 3 topics a chat. 12 chats: 3,633 tokens (112 lines) -> 1,487. recall.js:178 does call renderRange with its 10x10 defaults. Caveat: a day recall is the model asking for more. With a 3-topic cap, needing a 4th topic of a chat means a recall('c3') (375 tokens for a 10-topic chat) and one more request that re-sends the context as cached input. So the net gain depends on how often that happens. A token budget, as the other layers have, fits better than a fixed cap of 3._

title: ledger.json is rewritten whole on every turn of every chat, mostly zeros; meta.json stores a path nobody reads
body:
**Problem** (low)
Every turn adds requests and tool counts, so settle writes the whole ledger at every turn end of every chat, memory on or off. Each entry stores all 10 counters including zeros, an empty used list, and 'at'. Nothing reads 'at' (command.js and page.js read only c, used and msgs), and counters() already reads a missing key as 0. meta.json stores workspace: dirFor(agent), an absolute local path that no code reads (grep finds only writes). It is also a local path left in a folder users may sync.

**Where**: src/store/ledger.js:41-51 (addToLedger), src/host/builder.js:237-246 (settle), src/host/runtime.js:234 (meta.workspace)

**Evidence**
<scratch>/cg-c4-tokens/m11-ledger.mjs, 1,000 chats (80% with no memory activity): ledger.json 225,418 bytes; one turn-end write takes 6.7 ms. A quiet entry is 170 bytes, 65 without zero counters and the empty used list. Whole file: 141,418 bytes (-37%) without zeros and empty arrays, 109,418 (-51%) also without 'at'. m12-meta.mjs: a real meta is 344 bytes, of which workspace is 140 (204 without it).

**Fix**
Write only nonzero counters and non-empty arrays, drop 'at' and meta.workspace (old files still read fine). Optionally skip the turn-end write when the delta holds only requests/tool and fold it into the next write; the cost is a restart losing a few cached tool tokens from the estimate.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (tokens-quality lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Confirmed with the real addToLedger (v6-ledger.mjs), 1,000 chats, 80% quiet. ledger.json is 222,417 bytes; a quiet entry is 170 bytes and stores all 10 counters, used:[] and at. Dropping zero counters and empty used gives 138,417 bytes (-38%); also dropping at gives 106,417 (-52%). A turn-end write takes 7.3 ms median, off the critical path (it runs after the turn ends and nothing waits for it). Nothing reads at; command.js last.at is the build status. meta.workspace is written at runtime.js:234 and chats.js:225 and read nowhere. In a harness meta it is 104 of 307 bytes and holds the absolute path with the user name (<home>\...\.context-graph). Small storage gain, plus a privacy nit._

title: A damaged file that another program holds open is reported as set aside but is not. A memory-off chat then gets indexed, and damaged files get overwritten with no copy kept
body:
**Problem** (medium)
When JSON.parse fails, readJsonDetailed tries to move the file to `.corrupt-<time>` and swallows every rename error, assuming the only cause is ENOENT. On Windows, a program holding the file without delete sharing makes that rename fail with EBUSY. OneDrive and other sync tools or a virus scan do this, the same holds renameRetry was written for. The function still returns 'quarantined' and logs "kept as <aside>", but nothing was kept.
(a) loadMeta finds no `.corrupt` copy and returns undefined, so memoryOn and sharedOn both read true. For a non-fork chat, its own memory blocks, recall of other chats and the turn-end build all run as if memory were on. The builder computes its span from seq 0 with no gaps, so it reads the off stretch.
(b) The writers (saveMessages, the builder's loadGraph writable + saveGraph, addToLedger, updateMeta) start from an empty value. Once the hold ends within renameRetry's ~5 s, they overwrite the damaged file. Every earlier topic, message or ledger entry is gone, which breaks rule 5 and rule 7.

**Where**: src/store/files.js:66 (readJsonDetailed: `try { await rename(path, aside) } catch { /* another reader moved it first */ }`). Effects reach src/store/chats.js:65-72 (loadMeta), src/host/builder.js:90-122, src/store/messages.js:30, src/store/ledger.js:186 and src/store/chats.js:141.

**Evidence**
All probes are in <scratch>/cg-c4-freshbug/.
- hold-check.mjs: a file held with PowerShell [IO.File]::Open(..., 'ReadWrite', 'ReadWrite') still reads fine, but rename fails with EBUSY, 3 out of 3 times.
- locked-meta.mjs: a memory-off private meta.json with its tail cut. Not held: a fail-closed meta (memoryOn=false) and a `.corrupt` file. Held: loadMeta -> undefined, memoryOn=true, sharedOn=true, files=["meta.json"], and the log still says "kept as ...corrupt-...".
- locked-overwrite.mjs: msgs.json goes from 40 messages to 1 after saveMessages; topics.json goes from 25 topics to 1 through loadGraph(writable) + mergeDelta + saveGraph. No `.corrupt` copy is left in either case.
- host-offleak.mjs, through the real plugin and the test harness: a memory-off chat (offSeq 8, builtSeq 8) whose damaged meta.json is held for 2 s at turn end. Result: 1 builder call, and its prompt contained the turns typed while off ("SECRET my tax id is 123-45-6785"). msgs.json stored that text. meta.json was rewritten with builtSeq 16. The original meta has no `.corrupt` copy.

**Fix**
One line in the shared function: `try { await rename(path, aside) } catch (error) { if (error?.code !== 'ENOENT') throw error }`. Callers already treat a throw as "cannot read now": readChats skips the chat, addMemory and build catch it, and writers abort without writing. Quarantined reads are not cached, so the next read retries the move. As a second guard, build() could check memoryOn(meta) again after `if (!meta) meta = await rt.updateFor(...)` and recompute the span from that meta.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (bugs lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Reproduced. My own store probe (<scratch>/cg-c4-bugs/v0-store.mjs) used a memory-off meta.json with its tail cut. With no hold, loadMeta returns a fail-closed meta and a .corrupt copy appears. With the file held by PowerShell [IO.File]::Open(...,'ReadWrite','ReadWrite') (no Delete share), the rename at files.js:66 fails and the error is swallowed, but the log still says 'kept as ...corrupt-...'. loadMeta then returns undefined, memoryOn and sharedOn are both true, and the folder holds only meta.json. Writers under a 1 s hold: renameRetry waits it out and then overwrites. msgs.json goes 40 -> 1, topics.json (loadGraph writable + saveGraph) 25 -> 1, ledger.json 30 entries -> 1, with 0 .corrupt copies; without the hold each writer leaves a copy. End to end: I re-ran host-offleak.mjs with the resolve-dsh hook. 1 builder call whose prompt held the 'SECRET ...' off-str…_

title: Everyday messages with a time word and "we <verb>" get a day digest of about 360-470 tokens
body:
**Problem** (medium)
MEMORY_VERB includes present-tense verbs (do, use, try, plan, pick, say, build, write), and the bare `we X` alternative accepts them anywhere in the message. PAST_ZH also accepts the future 我们要讨论的.
So "what should we do tonight?" yields range = today, asksAboutPast = true and no topic hit, and memory.js appends renderRange of today's chats. The README says "A message that only mentions a day ... gets nothing" and "sends nothing for 20 of 20 everyday messages". The corpus's UNRELATED set has no such phrasing.
The identical block is not re-sent while it is on the surface, so this happens once per chat per range. But the block stays in context and is re-sent as cached input with every later request.

**Where**: src/core/time.js:67-69: PAST_EN's bare `we ${MEMORY_VERB}\b` alternative, and PAST_ZH's `(?:我们|咱们)[^。？?！!]{0,8}(?:聊|讨论|定|决定|说|谈)(?:过|了|的)`. Used at src/host/memory.js:130.

**Evidence**
- <scratch>/cg-c4-freshbug/digest.mjs, on the relevance corpus with 3 chats active today: 12 of 12 everyday messages got a digest, 4,497 tokens in all. That is 470 tokens each when chats were active then, 14 for '[context-graph] No indexed chats from last week.'. Examples: 'what should we do tonight?', 'should we try the new thai place today?', 'how do we use a french press? I want coffee this morning', 'this month we pick a new car, sedan or SUV?', '今天我们要讨论的是周末去哪玩'.
- host-digest.mjs, through the real plugin (test harness, 4 chats indexed today): 'what should we do tonight?' got a 357-token '[context-graph] Chats from today' block.

**Fix**
In PAST_EN, keep the base verbs only after did/have/had we and 'what did we'. Allow the bare form only in past tense after a relative word: `(?:what|which|how|why|where|when|that|the [\w-]+) we (?:already |just )?PAST_VERB`. In PAST_ZH, rule out 要/将/会/打算/准备 between 我们 and the verb.
Measured with past-fix.mjs: everyday messages flagged drop from 12/12 to 1/12. The one left, 这周我们说的读书计划, is arguably about earlier talk. The repo tests' 14 negatives stay at 0. All 15 memory questions are still caught (the tests' 9, plus 'remind me what we decided yesterday', 'the port we picked last week?', 'how we fixed the login bug yesterday', 今天我们讨论的方案是什么, 昨天我们定了哪个端口).

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (bugs lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Reproduced. In <scratch>/cg-c4-bugs/v1-past.mjs, parseTimeRange gives a range AND asksAboutPast returns true for these everyday messages: 'what should we do tonight?', 'should we try the new thai place today?', 'how do we use a french press? ... this morning', 'this month we pick a new car', 'today we write the release notes', 'can we fix the bike this week?' and '今天我们要讨论的是周末去哪玩'. The causes are the bare `we ${MEMORY_VERB}` alternative with present-tense verbs, and PAST_ZH's (?:过|了|的), which accepts 要讨论的. Real memory questions still match. Through the plugin (re-ran host-digest.mjs), 'what should we do tonight?' got a 357-token '[context-graph] Chats from today' block. Later messages with the same range got nothing, because the identical block is skipped while it is on the surface. The corpus probe re-run gives 12/12 and 4,497 tokens. 3 of those 12 are past-tense…_

title: A day's digest and recall("YYYY-MM-DD") list chats that merely span the day ahead of the chat actually worked on that day, which can go unnamed
body:
**Problem** (medium)
chatInRange is true for any chat started before the day and active after it. renderRange then orders those chats newest-first by lastActiveAt and keeps 3 for the digest (rangeMaxChats) or 10 for recall, naming at most 10 more by id. Long-running chats that a user keeps coming back to, which are common in large workspaces, fill every slot even though they have no topic from that day. The one chat worked on that day is not mentioned at all. The README promises '2026-11-01 → Every shared chat active that day, with its topics from that day'. The same applies to the digest memory.js sends for 'what did we do on <day>?'.

**Where**: src/core/render.js:142-158 (renderRange: newestFirst over chatInRange, then slice(0, maxChats), naming only 10 more ids) and src/core/time.js:84 (chatInRange).

**Evidence**
<scratch>/cg-c4-freshbug/dayrank.mjs, with dates built from local days so the result does not depend on time zone: 30 chats active Nov 1-17 (topics from Nov 1 and Nov 16), plus c40, worked on only on Nov 5 (3 topics that day).
- Digest for 2026-11-05: 82 tokens. It lists c8, c18 and c28, each '(2 topics)' with no topic lines. c40 is not named.
- recall("2026-11-05"): 169 tokens, 10 spanning chats, then '… 21 more chats (c12, c22, …)'. c40 is still not named.

**Fix**
Order chats by how many of their topics were updated in the range, then by lastActiveAt. Spanning chats can optionally be dropped when some chat has topics from then. With that order (dayrank-fix.mjs), the digest lists c40 first with its 3 topics, in 124 tokens.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (bugs lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Reproduced with my own probe, <scratch>/cg-c4-bugs/v2-day.mjs (dates built from local days). c9 was worked on only on Nov 5 and has 2 topics from that day. The other chats started Oct 20, were last active Nov 16, and have no topic from Nov 5. With just 3 such chats, the Nov-5 digest (maxChats 3) lists c103, c102 and c101, each '(2 topics)' with zero topic lines, and pushes c9 down to '... 1 more chats (c9)'. With 25 of them, neither the digest (82 tokens) nor recall('2026-11-05') (158 tokens) names c9 at all. Cause: chatInRange (time.js:84) checks only whether the chat's lifetime overlaps the day, and renderRange sorts by lastActiveAt, never by topics updated in the range. README line 233 promises 'with its topics from that day'._

title: /context-graph map writes every chat into the session log: about 1 MB per call at 1,000 chats
body:
**Problem** (low)
renderMap lists every chat with up to 8 topics each, including private chats and chats with no topics. dsh appends the handler's full text to the chat's session log as the command/done event (dsh-commands lib/index.js: settle → appendLifecycle('command/done', { text })). That happens on every invocation, and the card renders all of it as one pre-wrap body. The model never sees it, so the cost is log storage, session loading and the size of the card.

**Where**: src/host/command.js:90-93 and src/core/render.js:162-171 (renderMap)

**Evidence**
<scratch>/cg-c4-freshbug/bigmap.mjs (corpus copies, about 1 KB per chat):
- 150 chats: 151 KB, 1,351 lines
- 1,020 chats: 1,035 KB, 9,181 lines
- 1,500 chats: 1,524 KB, 13,501 lines

**Fix**
Cap the output at the newest ~40 chats and end with '… N more chats; Plugins → Context Graph has the full map'. That is about 41 KB and ~360 lines at any workspace size, 25-37x less at 1,020-1,500 chats.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (bugs lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Re-measured with <scratch>/cg-c4-bugs/v3-map.mjs: 151 KB / 1,352 lines at 151 views, 1,035 KB / 9,182 lines at 1,021, and 1,525 KB / 13,502 lines at 1,501. The first 50 chats alone are 49 KB, so a cap gives about a 20x cut at 1,000 chats. Confirmed in dsh-commands lib/index.js: settle() appends { text: result.text } as a command/done event on every call, and I found no size cap. Caveat: dsh-session-persistence-jsonl compresses session logs with zstd by default (DEFAULT_COMPRESSION = 'zstd'), so the cost on disk is below the raw size (v3-zstd.mjs). The corpus copies compress 50x only because they repeat; unique map text compressed only 1.6x in a 5 KB sample. The decoded event and the card stay full size. The command only runs when the user types it, hence low._

title: Every turn end in any chat rewrites the whole workspace ledger.json
body:
**Problem** (low)
For every turn end of every tracked chat (its requests and tool counters are never zero), addToLedger reads ledger.json without the cache, then parses it, stringifies it and rewrites all of it. On a large workspace the parse and stringify block the event loop that streams the other chats, and the file is re-uploaded by sync tools on every turn.

**Where**: src/store/ledger.js:184-194 (addToLedger), called from src/host/builder.js settle()

**Evidence**
<scratch>/cg-c4-freshbug/bigledger.mjs, with 1,500 chat entries:
- Light (5 used ids and 10 message keys per chat): ledger.json is 530 KB; 18.1 ms per turn end, 12.6 ms of it synchronous parse+stringify.
- Busy (40 / 100): 2,341 KB; 47.7 ms per turn end, 37.2 ms of it blocking.
- One chat's entry is 362 B (light) or 1,598 B (busy).

**Fix**
Keep one small file per chat, for example <dir>/ledger/<sid>.json, so no chat folder is needed, written under the same lock. The chat entry comes from that one file. The workspace total sums stat-keyed cached reads of those files, which only the card and the page need. The current ledger.json is read once as the migration source. Each turn end then writes 0.4-1.6 KB instead of 0.5-2.3 MB, with no whole-ledger parse on the event loop.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (bugs lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: Re-measured with <scratch>/cg-c4-bugs/v4-ledger.mjs (2 runs, 1,500 entries). A 532 KB ledger takes 13-17 ms per addToLedger, 11-12.5 ms of it synchronous parse+stringify. A 2,155 KB ledger takes 46-53 ms, 34-39 ms synchronous. Writing one chat's 323 B or 1,431 B entry on its own takes 1.4-1.9 ms. Every main request bumps st.delta.requests and tool (meter.js:37-40), so settle writes at every turn end. The item's line numbers are wrong: addToLedger is store/ledger.js:41-52. The gain is real but small: the write is off the critical path and documented as once per turn, and splitting the file would make workspace totals cost many small reads._

title: parseTimeRange understands only 5 of 19 common ways of naming a past day, and gets 大前天 and 上上周 wrong
body:
**Problem** (low)
Only digits are accepted before 'days ago' or 天前. There is no handling of weeks ago, last night, weekday names or English month names. 大前天 matches 前天, giving -2 instead of -3, and 上上周 matches 上周, giving last week instead of the week before. Without a range, a time question gets neither the time ranking nor the day digest.

**Where**: src/core/time.js:35-61 (parseTimeRange)

**Evidence**
<scratch>/cg-c4-freshbug/timewords.mjs: 0.9.0 gets 5 of 19 right. It misses 'two days ago', 'a week ago', 'last night', 'on monday', 'nov 3', 'november 3rd', '2 weeks ago', 三天前, 两天前, 一周前 and 两周前, and returns the wrong day or week for 大前天 and 上上周.
timewords-fix.mjs, a ~25-line pre-pass that falls through to the current parser: 18 of 19 right (only 'a few days ago' is left on purpose). It invents a range for 0 of 5 time-free messages ('may I ask a question', 'one day I want to visit japan', 'the march of progress', 'a few more tests please', 一天到晚都在改bug).

**Fix**
Add the pre-pass in front of parseTimeRange: English and Chinese number words, N days/weeks ago and N天/周/个星期前, last night, on/last <weekday> (the most recent past one), English month names with an optional ordinal (the past occurrence), 大前天 = -3, and 上上周 = the week before last week. It is most useful together with the digest ordering fix.

_Found by the cycle-4 audit of 0.9.0 (bugs lens) and confirmed by an independent verifier: The 'before' is confirmed (re-ran timewords.mjs): 5 of 19. Two of the misses are outright wrong ranges: 大前天 -> 'the day before yesterday' (day -2, should be -3), and 上上周 -> last week starting at day -8 (should be day -15 for Tue Nov 17 2026). The claimed 'after' is overstated. The candidate's month rule `(jan|...|dec)[a-z]*` matches any word that starts with a month abbreviation. On 10 time-free messages of my own (<scratch>/cg-c4-bugs/v5-run.mjs) it invented a date for 8: 'we decided 3 things' -> 2025-12-03, 'the decision 2' -> 2025-12-02, 'junior 2' -> June 2, 'market 5' / 'mark 3' / 'markdown 2' -> March, 'separate 2' -> Sep 2, 'novel 2' -> Nov 2. Because the pre-pass runs first, it also overrode a real 'yesterday' ('what did we decide yesterday, we decided 3 options' -> 2025-12-03). With whole month names only (v5-run2.mjs), all 8 go away and 'nov 3' / 'novem…_
